subtype: Approach: working backward from the target employer [Thinking]
passage:
Francis: ok I looked at the last 10 job posts from the 3 firms I want
Francis: they keep saying "built and deployed", "worked with real data", "owns a feature end to end"
Chaitanya: so not "made a calculator" 😅
Francis: exactly. So my plan: 2 projects. One that cleans and analyses messy data, one that's live on the internet with a real link
Chaitanya: What about the other 8 you were going to do?
Francis: Dropping them. Recruiters won't open ten. I would rather they open two and stay
Chaitanya: Which first?
Francis: The data one. I have the bus-timings data already. 3 weeks
Chaitanya: Send me the link when it's up 🙂

qa.q: How many projects did Francis decide to build?
What is Francis feeling about dropping the other eight projects?
qa.a: Francis feels focused and relieved, saying it is better to have two that recruiters open than ten they skip.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Francis add, and why?
qa.a: Francis could ask a recruiter or an alumnus at those firms what impresses them, because job posts show wording but a person can say what actually gets a project opened.

qa.q: How does Chaitanya see Francis's plan?
qa.a: Chaitanya jokes about calculators, asks what happens to the other eight and asks for the link, so Chaitanya seems supportive and curious.

grounding: Shows planning a portfolio backward from what target employers ask to see, choosing a few substantial projects.
